title: 備忘錄與最重要的事
en: Memos and the Most Important Thing

vocab.example: Oaktree Capital Management, the company I cofounded in 1995.
vocab.def: co- 是「共同」，cofound 就是和別人一起創立公司。課文寫的是過去式 cofounded，作者與夥伴一起創辦了 Oaktree。
vocab.exzh: 橡樹資本管理公司，也就是我在 1995 年共同創辦的公司。

vocab.example: I use the memos to set forth my investment philosophy, explain the workings of finance and provide my take on recent events.
vocab.def: 比較正式的說法，指有條理地把想法或主張寫出來、說清楚。
vocab.exzh: 我用這些備忘錄來闡述我的投資哲學、說明金融運作的道理，並提出我對近期事件的看法。

vocab.example: provide my take on recent events
vocab.def: my take on 就是「我對…的看法」，語氣比 opinion 隨性。這裡的 take 是名詞，不是「拿」。
vocab.exzh: 提出我對近期事件的看法

vocab.example: I believe their lessons apply as well today as they did when they were written.
vocab.def: 這裡不是「申請」，而是指教訓、道理在現在依然「適用」。
vocab.exzh: 我相信這些教訓在今天依然適用，就像它們被寫下來的當時一樣。

vocab.example: For inclusion here I’ve made some minor changes, primarily to make their message clearer.
vocab.def: 與 major 相對，minor changes 指只是小修小改，沒有動到內容。
vocab.exzh: 收進這本書時，我做了一些小幅修改，主要是為了讓訊息更清楚。

vocab.example: As I meet with clients and prospects, I repeatedly hear myself say, ‘The most important thing is X.’
vocab.def: 在業務領域，prospects 指還沒成交、但有可能成為客戶的人。它也可以指「前景」，要看上下文。
vocab.exzh: 我在與客戶和潛在客戶見面時，一再聽見自己說：『最重要的事是 X。』

vocab.example: a memo with that title that pulled together the elements I felt were essential for investment success
vocab.def: 比 important 更強，表示少了它就不行。後面常接 for / to。
vocab.exzh: 一份用這個標題寫成的備忘錄，把我認為對投資成功不可或缺的要素整合在一起

vocab.example: the fundamental notion is unchanged: they’re all important
vocab.def: 指最底層、不會輕易改變的東西。fundamental notion 就是「根本的概念」。
vocab.exzh: 根本的概念沒有改變：它們全都很重要

vocab.example: I’ve made a few adjustments in the things I consider “the most important,”
vocab.def: 小幅度的修改。作者承認自己的清單有微調，但核心沒變。
vocab.exzh: 我對那些我認為「最重要」的事做了幾項調整，

vocab.example: Omit any one and the result is likely to be less than satisfactory.
vocab.def: 把本來該有的東西漏掉。比 leave out 正式。
vocab.exzh: 漏掉任何一項，結果就可能不夠令人滿意。

vocab.example: each is a brick in what I hope will be a solid wall, and none is dispensable.
vocab.def: indispensable（不可或缺）的反義詞。課文用 none is dispensable，表示每一項都不能少。
vocab.exzh: 每一項都是一塊磚，我希望它們能砌成一道堅實的牆，而且沒有一塊是可有可無的。

sentences.en: For the last twenty years I’ve been writing occasional memos to my clients—first at Trust Company of the West and then at Oaktree Capital Management, the company I cofounded in 1995.
sentences.zh: 過去二十年來，我不定期地寫備忘錄給我的客戶——先是在西部信託公司，後來是在橡樹資本管理公司，那是我在 1995 年共同創辦的公司。

sentences.en: I use the memos to set forth my investment philosophy, explain the workings of finance and provide my take on recent events.
sentences.zh: 我用這些備忘錄來闡述我的投資哲學、說明金融運作的道理，並提出我對近期事件的看法。

sentences.en: Those memos form the core of this book, and you will find passages from many of them in the pages that follow, for I believe their lessons apply as well today as they did when they were written.
sentences.zh: 這些備忘錄是本書的核心，你會在後面的篇章裡讀到其中許多段落，因為我相信，這些教訓在今天依然適用，就像它們被寫下來的當時一樣。

sentences.en: For inclusion here I’ve made some minor changes, primarily to make their message clearer.
sentences.zh: 收進這本書時，我做了一些小幅修改，主要是為了讓訊息更清楚。

sentences.en: What, exactly, is “the most important thing”?
sentences.zh: 那麼，「最重要的事」到底是什麼？

sentences.en: In July 2003, I wrote a memo with that title that pulled together the elements I felt were essential for investment success.
sentences.zh: 2003 年 7 月，我寫了一份以此為題的備忘錄，把我認為對投資成功不可或缺的要素整合在一起。

sentences.en: Here’s how it began: “As I meet with clients and prospects, I repeatedly hear myself say, ‘The most important thing is X.’
sentences.zh: 開頭是這樣寫的：「我在與客戶和潛在客戶見面時，一再聽見自己說：『最重要的事是 X。』

sentences.en: And then ten minutes later it’s, ‘The most important thing is Y.’
sentences.zh: 然後十分鐘後又變成：『最重要的事是 Y。』

sentences.en: And then Z, and so on.”
All told, the memo ended up discussing eighteen “most important things.”
sentences.zh: 總計，這份備忘錄最後談了十八項「最重要的事」。

sentences.en: Since that original memo, I’ve made a few adjustments in the things I consider “the most important,” but the fundamental notion is unchanged: they’re all important.
sentences.zh: 自從那份原始備忘錄之後，我對自己認為「最重要」的事做了幾項調整，但根本的概念沒有變：它們全都很重要。

sentences.en: Successful investing requires thoughtful attention to many separate aspects, all at the same time.
sentences.zh: 成功的投資需要同時對許多不同面向都用心關注。

sentences.en: Omit any one and the result is likely to be less than satisfactory.
sentences.zh: 漏掉任何一項，結果就可能不夠令人滿意。

sentences.en: That is why I have built this book around the idea of the most important things—each is a brick in what I hope will be a solid wall, and none is dispensable.
sentences.zh: 這就是我為什麼把這本書圍繞著「最重要的事」這個概念來架構——每一項都是一塊磚，我希望它們能砌成一道堅實的牆，而且沒有一塊是可有可無的。

grammar.quote: Omit any one and the result is likely to be less than satisfactory.
grammar.explain:
Omit any one 是祈使句（動詞原形開頭），後面接 and 再接一個完整子句，意思相當於 If you omit any one, the result is likely to be…。
這是很常見的省力寫法，例如 Study hard and you’ll pass. 讀到「祈使句＋and＋結果」，就當成條件句來理解。

grammar.point: as well … as：同等比較，後半用代動詞
grammar.quote: I believe their lessons apply as well today as they did when they were written.
grammar.explain:
as well today as they did 是「和…一樣好」的同等比較。後面的 did 代替前面的 applied，避免重複動詞。
整句的意思是：這些教訓現在適用的程度，和當初寫下它們的時候一樣。

grammar.point: 插入語 I hope：夾在 what 子句中間
grammar.quote: each is a brick in what I hope will be a solid wall
grammar.explain:
what will be a solid wall 是名詞子句，作 in 的受詞。中間夾了 I hope，是插入語，表示說話者的心態，拿掉也不影響句子結構。
類似用法還有 what I think is…、what he says is…，讀的時候先把插入語略過，句子就通了。
